content.title: Children's Reading Day
content.subtitle: Celebrating and promoting literacy in primary schools in Turiani, Tanzania
content.summary: Celebrating and promoting literacy in primary schools in Turiani, Tanzania

content.text: The excitement among the school-aged children was palpable: where there was storytelling, music, dance, reading, writing, there were also a lot of wide grins, nods and running around. Needless to say, the Children's Reading Day in the town of Turiani, located around 200 km away from the capital city of Dar es Salaam, was a change from their regular Friday at school.

Jointly organized by the Room To Read Foundation and the AKU Institute for Educational Development, East Africa, the event aimed to provide a creative platform for children to interact with books and engage in literary activities. Initially, invitations were sent to 15 schools part of the Awali Reads Project, a partnership between Room to Read and IED, EA. On the day of the event, over 700 people showed up - while nearly 500 of them were schoolchildren who were accompanied by primary school teachers and community volunteers from each of the project schools, there were also other important figures such as village leaders, parents and district and regional government education officers.
If anything, it points to the positive impact of the project to create an interest and mobilise the local community.
The day was led by AKU member of faculty and project lead Dr Lillian Vikiru along with current students from IED, EA's MEd programme and Room to Read staff in Tanzania.
